title: Fibre care: silk and silk blends
subtitle: Washing, drying, and storing crochet worked in silk or silk-blend yarn
excerpt: Silk is the strongest natural fibre but also the most damaged by heat and rough handling. A silk crochet piece needs hand-washing in cool water, no wringing, no tumble drying, and drying flat away from direct sunlight. Silk blends follow the more delicate of the two fibres.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, 1886, Project Gutenberg #20776. Weldon's Practical Crochet, 1880s to 1900s, Internet Archive. Contemporary fibre care references.

glossaryTerms.definition: A natural protein fibre from the cocoon of the Bombyx mori silkworm. Smooth, lustrous, and strong when dry, but significantly weaker when wet. Very sensitive to heat and alkalis.
A fibre made from protein: silk and wool are the main examples. Protein fibres are damaged by alkaline detergents and high heat. They should be washed with a pH-neutral or slightly acid detergent.

content.text: Silk
is a
protein fibre

. It is strong in normal conditions but weakens significantly when wet, making it vulnerable to damage during washing. It also degrades under heat and strong alkalis. A silk crochet piece handles washing well if the steps are followed; the damage happens when it is wrung, heated, or exposed to direct sunlight while damp.
Washing
Fill a basin with cool water, 20 to 30°C. Hot water weakens silk and can cause permanent water marks.
Add a small amount of pH-neutral or silk-specific detergent. Standard wool washes are fine; laundry detergents are usually too alkaline.
Submerge the piece and gently squeeze the water through it. Do not rub, wring, or twist. The fabric weakens by up to 20% when wet.
Rinse twice in clean water at the same temperature. A sudden change in water temperature can set wrinkles permanently.
Lift the piece from the water with both hands, supporting its full weight. Never lift by one corner while wet.
Drying
Lay the piece between two clean towels and roll the towel gently. Press down to absorb excess moisture. Do not wring the towel roll.
Lay the piece flat on a dry towel or blocking mat. Ease it back to the correct shape while damp.
Dry at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Sunlight fades silk and can cause permanent yellowing. Do not use a tumble dryer or place on a heated towel rail.
Silk blends

Silk-wool, silk-cotton, and silk-linen blends are common. When washing a blend, follow the care requirements of whichever fibre is more delicate. A silk-wool blend should be washed as silk (cool water, no wringing); a silk-cotton blend can tolerate slightly warmer water than pure silk but still needs gentle handling.
Storage

Store silk crochet folded in acid-free tissue paper in a drawer away from light. Avoid hanging silk garments for long periods; the weight of the fabric pulls the shoulders and distorts the shape. Cedar blocks or lavender sachets repel moths without the chemical damage of mothballs.
Common problems

items.symptom: The piece has water spots or dark rings after drying
items.cause: Water that contains minerals (hard water) dries with a residue that marks silk. Or the water temperature was uneven across the piece while drying.
items.fix: Re-wet the whole piece in clean, cool water and allow it to dry completely and evenly. For recurring water marks, use filtered or distilled water for the final rinse.

items.symptom: The silk has lost its sheen after washing
items.cause: An alkaline detergent was used, which damages the outer protein layer of the fibre.
items.fix: A final rinse with a small amount of white vinegar (1 tablespoon per litre of rinse water) can restore some of the lustre by rebalancing the pH. This is a traditional dressing method, not a permanent fix.

items.cause: The water was too warm, or the piece was wrung.
items.fix: Wet the piece again in cool water and gently ease it back to its original dimensions while damp. Silk can be eased back to a surprising degree if handled carefully.

content.text: What to try next

Wash a gauge swatch in the intended silk yarn before starting a garment. This confirms how the yarn behaves when washed and whether it changes colour, loses sheen, or changes in dimensions. Block the swatch after washing to get accurate post-wash gauge measurements.
